messages:
incident-bot: Paging: CRITICAL — OrionFin (VPC-Private) reports inability to egress to Redwood model endpoints. Error rate spike detected, >95% of outbound connections failing (TCP RST / connection timeout). Auto-alert from egress-monitoring at 12:03 UTC.

sam oncall: ack — I'm on it, pausing non-essential pages.

sam oncall: quick summary from the customer: all app instances in private subnets can't reach api.redwood-infer.internal:443. They see timeouts or immediate RST. No alerts on ingress NLB.

jess platform: is this across AZs or single-AZ?

dave cs: customer says affects both AZs but only hosts in their private subnets; other tenants using same Dedicated pool unaffected.

raj netops: initial hypothesis: NAT connection-tracking exhaustion or a routing issue. I'm pulling NATGW and route table metrics.

kira infra: grabbing NAT metrics now — CloudWatch: NAT-gtw-orf-1 shows high ActiveConnections ~ 65500 and Surges in ConnectionErrors in the last 10m. Looks like connection-tracking at the appliance level hitting limits.

sam oncall: can you paste the cloudwatch snippet?

kira infra: ```
# CloudWatch snippet (last 5m)
NatGatewayId: nat-0a1b2c3d4e
ActiveConnections: 65784
ErrorPortAllocation: 423
PacketDropCount: 1120
ThroughputMbps: 120
```

raj netops: OK that fits conntrack exhaustion. For reference, when conntrack is exhausted new TCP sessions are dropped and you get timeouts/RST. That matches the customer's symptoms.

sam oncall: customer traffic pattern — any sudden surge? dave?
\ dave cs: They ran a scheduled batch job at 11:58 UTC that fan-outed many parallel model calls (they apologize). Likely coincident.

jess platform: Are there security group / NACL errors? I checked the VPC NACLs — no denies. SGs are allow-everything-outbound by default. So root cause seems NAT saturation.

raj netops: Steps to mitigate (short term): 1) attach an extra NAT Gateway in same AZ, 2) update customer's route table to point to new NAT, 3) if route swap can't be fast, we can add a temporary proxy instance (t3.large) with source/dest check disabled and snat to eip and update route.

sam oncall: Which is faster? creating NATGW or spinning a proxy? NATGW creation is quick but propagation and elastic IP allocation might take 60-90s. Proxy instance bootstrap may be ~5min. I vote NATGW first, fallback to proxy.

kira infra: I'm creating another NAT in the affected AZ now and allocating an EIP. Will post the NAT id when ready.

deploy-bot: Note: customer has a route table rtb-0f1e2d3c linked to private subnet subnet-0b2c3d4e. Any route change will affect all instances in that subnet. Confirming with customer for maintenance window (they already agreed to emergency).

kira infra: new nat created: nat-0f9e8d7c, EIP eip-54.23.12.8.

raj netops: I'm prepping replace-route command now. Once you confirm I will execute.

sam oncall: go for it.

raj netops: executing: ```bash
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0f1e2d3c --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0f9e8d7c
```

raj netops: route replaced, waiting for propagation.

sam oncall: testing from a customer host via their bastion (they provided safe access):
```bash
# from bastion
curl -v https://api.redwood-infer.internal/health
* TCP connection to 34.210.33.77 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Closing connection 0
curl: (7) Failed to connect to api.redwood-infer.internal port 443: Connection timed out
```

kira infra: can you retry after 30s, DNS TTL low but route propagation might take a bit.

sam oncall: retrying...
```bash
# after route swap
curl -v https://api.redwood-infer.internal/health
* Connected to 34.210.33.77 (34.210.33.77) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok"}
```

sam oncall: customer confirms traffic flows restored, error rate back to normal.

dave cs: OrionFin confirms their job resumed and finished successfully. They're extremely grateful.

jess platform: intermediate mitigation done. Next actions: - verify no stateful leaks on the old NAT, - schedule permanent capacity increase/second NAT for that VPC (or suggest AWS PrivateLink for model endpoint to avoid NAT), - create postmortem and recommend rate-limiting/backoff in customer's batch job.

raj netops: Agree. Also adding alerting thresholds for ActiveConnections > 60k for NATGW to trigger earlier paging.

sam oncall: I'll own the incident postmortem & customer-facing RCA. Will include timeline, root cause (conntrack exhaustion on NAT gateway due to high concurrent outbound sockets from OrionFin batch job), short-term mitigation (route swapped to new NATGW), and recommended long-term mitigations (per-tenant NATs, egress pooling, rate-limits, PrivateLink peering).

kira infra: I'll open an infra ticket to ensure we have runbook steps and automation to spin additional NAT gateways and update RTs with minimal blast radius.

dave cs: I'll follow up with OrionFin to offer guidance on client-side exponential backoff and to coordinate a post-incident review.

sam oncall: closing the incident thread once postmortem draft is ready. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged resolved by sam oncall at 12:17 UTC. Severity: HIGH. Tags: vpc-private, natgw, conntrack, tenant-isolation, customer-impact
